source.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
source.paraphrase: Mouret and Clune describe mapping strong solutions across user-chosen variation dimensions rather than returning only one overall winner; that framing motivates testing cell coverage, not predicting this callback's performance.

research.mechanism_explanation: MAP-Elites' descriptor-map idea motivates treating each eligible rotation-feature pair as a synthetic cell and giving each cell one proposal turn before revisiting streams. The callback sorts those cells, rotates the starting point by seed, traverses streams round-robin, and skips repeated canonical JSON payloads. It does not observe or rank candidate quality; the paper motivates a coverage test, not a performance claim.
research.hypothesis: Across the two development inputs and four paired seeds, at equal completed-call targets, breadth-first proposals across eligible rotation-feature cells will yield a higher mean unique-valid-cell count than synthetic_uniform_pair_selector_v1.
research.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified for this bounded development series if complete equal-call pairs produce a mean challenger-minus-reference unique-valid-cell difference of zero or less. An incomplete pair leaves that contrast unresolved rather than counting as a tie.

human_review.summary: Across four complete paired development runs, each arm completed 4 evaluator calls. Challenger-minus-reference unique-cell differences were 0, +1, +1, and +2 (mean +1); synthetic quality-pass differences were +1, 0, +1, and -1. These descriptive fixture results make no live, out-of-sample, server-acceptance, or genetic-performance claim.
human_review.rationale: The callback applies the paper's map-oriented search intuition by spreading proposals over rotation-feature cells before revisiting a stream. It uses deterministic ordering and duplicate suppression, not an elite archive or quality-based selection, because candidate labels belong to the evaluator. The development comparison supports the coverage hypothesis on these specific synthetic inputs, while the mixed quality-bit differences and small fixture scope argue against broader inference.
